title: migrate corrupts single-file configs (e.g. .pretender.toml becomes directory symlink)
description:
When legacy_path.is_file(), migrate_tool() symlinks to the tool's directory (.ddl/pretender/) not the file inside it. Any subsequent read hits EISDIR. unmigrate_tool() creates_dir_all(legacy_path) on what was originally a file, turning .pretender.toml into a directory.

Source: src/dot_ddl.rs:migrate_tool() and unmigrate_tool()

Fix: For file migration, target should be ddl_tool_path.join(legacy_path.file_name()). For undo, detect original type before create_dir_all.
close_reason: Fixed in commit b7f5333 (old ID DDL-el9, same-day fix 2026-08-05): migrate_tool() tracks legacy_path_was_file, moves file into .ddl/<tool>/, symlinks to the file inside; unmigrate_tool() detects original type via read_link before restoring. Verified: all 11 tests in tests/migrate.rs pass, incl. single-file corruption and undo cases. Ticket was left open after beads→Dolt ID re-key.

title: Normalize migration paths so migrate --undo detects symlinks

close_reason: Fixed: migrated_tools resolves relative symlink targets to absolute and canonicalizes both resolved and expected paths before comparing, handling both directory and single-file symlink patterns.

title: P0: Add behavioral guardrails to AGENTS.md — Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers
description:
## Finding (from Agent Value Alignment audit)

AGENTS.md provides workflow instructions (wai → beads → openspec, TDD, session discipline) but **no behavioral guardrails**. An AI assistant working on this repo has no guidance on what it should/shouldn't do beyond the workflow.

### What's missing

- **Goal Sandwich**: The primary objective must appear verbatim at top AND bottom of the prompt (lost-in-the-middle countermeasure)
- **Prohibited behaviors (negations)**: 5 explicit "DON'T:" statements — e.g., DON'T make breaking changes without an openspec proposal, DON'T skip tests, DON'T refactor without test coverage
- **Escalation triggers**: The 7 named types — when to stop and ask (uncertainty, scope boundary, resource limit, anomaly detection, human review trigger, conflicting instructions, high stakes)
- **Minimal Footprint clause**: Resource/side-effect constraints for the assistant
- **Drift detection**: Self-check loop (ALIGNMENT check before major actions)

Your AGENTS.md is the strongest in the suite (context boundary warning, autonomous work policy) — but still missing: Goal Sandwich, explicit prohibitions, 7 escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint clause.

### What to do

1. Add a Goal Sandwich: objective statement in first 5 lines AND last 5 lines of the AGENTS.md prompt area
2. Add a "## Prohibited" section with 5+ explicit DON'T statements
3. Add a "## Stop and Ask" section with escalation triggers
4. Add a "## Minimal Footprint" clause
5. If eval tests exist, add a note about behavioral regression; if not, file a follow-up

### Priority rationale (P0)

Without behavioral guardrails, assistant behavior is unconstrained — the most common failure mode for AI-assisted development is scope creep and silent drift.

### References
- agent-value-alignment skill: references/layer-3-runtime-prompt.md
- Full audit report: genesis-ntg (genesis repo)

Also fixed wai-specific: removed .wai/projects/ from prohibited artifacts. Fixed dulce-de-leche: replaced unverifiable cross-compilation DON'T. Fixed espectacular: added DON'T about parallel genesis types. Fixed dont: added genesis donor note.

title: `migrate` corrupts single-file configs (`.pretender.toml`)
description:
**File:** `src/dot_ddl.rs:migrate_tool()`

When `legacy_path.is_file()`, the symlink is created pointing to the directory
(`.ddl/pretender/`) instead of the file, corrupting the config.

**Fix:**
```rust
// CORRECT (for file migration):
std::os::unix::fs::symlink(
    ddl_tool_path.join(legacy_path.file_name().unwrap_or_default()),
    legacy_path,
)
```
notes: Co-modifies src/dot_ddl.rs with 5 other eval ticket(s): DDL-cbp, DDL-el9, DDL-40e, DDL-npg, DDL-sl0, DDL-ttg. Coordinate/rebase if picking up in parallel.

title: Tool-init cascade: failures are warnings, ordering is wrong, not idempotent-until-green (bajan needed 3 runs)
description:
bajan 9/28 (ddl 0.5.0): single 'ddl init -y' emitted a half-failed cascade and still exited ok:
- 'dont init exited 1: no .dont/ project found — run dont init first' (circular ordering)
- 'ah init exited 1: openspec/ directory not found' (ah ran before openspec existed)
- 'vampiro not found on PATH — skipping init' (downloaded to ~/.ddl/bin which is not on PATH; init prints a hint but never applies/installs it)
- 'fotos-mcp init exited 1: Error: expect initialize request' (tool has no init; ddl should skip it)
Agent re-ran 'ddl init -y' 3 times, then manually ran 'dont init' + PATH setup. Failures render as warnings with exit 0, so nothing stops early and the repo is left half-configured.

Fix: prerequisite-ordered cascade (openspec before ah; PATH applied or bin dir self-registered before initing downloaded tools; skip tools without init); failures fail the init (or a 'resume' summary lists exactly what is still missing + the exact command to finish); interactive prompt text must not leak into -y output (pretender's 'Mode (guidance/tiered/gate) [tiered]:' appeared in non-interactive output — ambiguous whether defaults applied).
acceptance_criteria: ddl init -y on fresh repo converges in ONE run or exits non-zero; resume re-run applies only missing steps; no prompt text in -y output; tools without init are skipped silently

title: Binary install: GitHub API 403 rate limiting — no token support, poor error message
description: Found by smoke run 35021913998 (macos-latest): 'ddl install turu' failed with 'GitHub API returned 403 Forbidden for https://api.github.com/repos/charly-vibes/whisper/releases/latest'. Unauthenticated api.github.com is limited to 60 req/hr per IP; GitHub-hosted runners share IPs, so the limit is routinely exhausted. Fixes: (1) send Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN when the env var is present (Actions runners always have one; also helps CI users); (2) treat 403 with rate-limit headers as a distinct error naming the limit and remedy, not a generic failure; (3) consider falling back to the releases/latest redirect URL (github.com/REPO/releases/latest/download/...) which avoids the API entirely for the asset path. Related: DDL-ei3 binary-first chain reliability. Files: src/installer.rs

title: Windows install: os error 33 (file locked) after binary download
description: Found by smoke run 35021913998 (windows-latest): 'ddl install turu' downloaded turu.exe successfully ('turu downloaded to %LOCALAPPDATA%/ddl/bin/turu.exe') then failed with 'IO error: The process cannot access the file because another process has locked a portion of the file. (os error 33)'. Freshly-written executables on Windows are commonly locked transiently by Defender/AV scanning. Needs investigation of the post-download path (ensure_on_path / manifest write / run_tool_init) to find which operation hit the lock; likely fix is a bounded retry-with-backoff around the affected operation. Blocks 3-platform close of DDL-9c2 and DDL-ei3. Files: src/installer.rs
close_reason: Root cause: LockFileEx same-process self-deadlock, fixed by single-handle manifest writes (PR #9); Windows smoke green (35028164994)

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: Root cause found by code reading (not AV!): Manifest::save reopened the manifest under a fs2 LockFileEx lock held by another handle — Windows byte-range locks block same-process handles, deterministic ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION. Fixed via single-handle read-modify-write (PRs #5, #8, #9 — #9 is the root-cause fix). Verified: Windows smoke green end-to-end (run 35028164994).

title: Simplify install policy: binary-first, cargo fallback; remove brew/scoop from method selection

DECISION (user, 2026-09-15 session): ddl installs prebuilt binaries first on ALL platforms; cargo is the fallback when binary is unavailable and cargo is installed; npm remains only for incitaciones. brew/scoop are removed from best_install_method() decision path — tap formulas/scoop manifests stay published as ecosystem infra for manual installs, but no longer influence ddl.

- macOS: brew first (if formula real, via is_placeholder_formula) -> cargo -> binary
- Linux: cargo first -> binary
- Windows: scoop first -> binary (no cargo fallback at all)

- Binary (release asset) when it exists, on every platform
- Fallback: cargo install (crate_name) when binary missing (404) AND cargo available
- If neither: clear error naming both prerequisites
- incitaciones: npm unchanged

- Update module header docs (NOTE: old spec said report error rather than fall back on 404 — this decision reverses that), README install section, docs/ecosystem-map.md
